title: Young Adults Find It Difficult to Make Friends — Survey
paragraphs: Many young adults find it hard to make new friends, according to a new survey in the US.

The survey was done by Talker Research for Life Time, a fitness company. In October 2026, it asked 1,000 members of Gen Z about their social lives. Gen Z are people who were born between the late 1990s and the early 2010s.

The survey found that 52% of the young people had trouble making new friends. Also, 69% said that they felt lonelier than they had expected to feel as adults. On average, the young people had three close friends, but 43% had fewer than that.
Many of them want to change this. About 73% said they want to spend more time with other people, and 71% said they want to make new friends.

So, what is stopping them? Money was the biggest problem. About 37% said that going out costs too much. Time is another problem. Around 30% said they are too tired after work or school, and 69% said they do not have time to go out.

Many young people also said they need a "third space." This is a place that is not home, work or school, where people can meet others. About 60% agreed that they need a third space to make friends. However, many said that coffee shops and bars do not meet their needs.
The survey also found that 73% believe it would be easier to find friends in person. Life Time suggests that gyms and fitness classes could be a good place for young people to meet new friends.
